thread:
mia: FYI deploybot flagged SBOM noise for rc-2026-c. Change window now (10:00-12:00 PT). We need a delegated approver to avoid blocking the canary. @jorge can infra-oncall take low-license approvals?

deploybot: SCAN rc-2026-c summary:
- critical: 0
- high: 0
- medium: 1 (transitive pkg-x@2.4.0)
- low: 2 (license tags: two entries)
Gate: manual approval required. SBOM diff: https://artifacts/internal/rc-2026-c/sbom/diff

jorge: We can approve low-license items from oncall if licenses are on procurement_whitelist AND there are no failing tests in staging. Will require oncall to paste evidence and SHA in thread.

hannah: Security: for the medium transitive, we need CVSS + observed exploitability. If CVSS < 6 and no evidence of exploit, allow with mitigation ticket and 90-minute canary watch. If CVSS >= 6 or exploitability present -> block until Security review.

security-bot: lookup pkg-x@2.4.0 -> CVSS 4.8, exploitability low. Recommend allow with mitigation ticket INF-4500.

mia: agreed. Decision: 1) infra-oncall can approve low-license noise during the change window with evidence in-thread; 2) medium transitive pkg-x allowed due to CVSS 4.8 with mitigation INF-4500 and a 90-minute canary guard; 3) deploybot should append approval metadata to the artifact manifest for audit.

deploybot: will attach fields to artifact manifest. example metadata lines:
approved_by: "jorge-oncall"
approval_method: "oncall-delegation"
approval_evidence: "https://artifacts/internal/rc-2026-c/sbom/diff"
approval_ts: "2026-09-15T10:07:00Z"
mitigation_ticket: "INF-4500"
canary_guard_minutes: "90"
rollback_condition: "cvss>=6 || canary_alerts==true"
release_note_line: "rc-2026-c: infra-oncall delegated approval for low license noise; pkg-x@2.4.0 allowed with mitigation INF-4500; canary 90m."

jorge: approved via oncall UI. artifact sha: sha256:feedfacecafebeef0102030405060708; evidence: https://artifacts/internal/rc-2026-c/sbom/diff; approval_ts: 2026-09-15T10:08:12Z. Pasted evidence in thread.

hannah: Security will instrument guards and alert on anomalous traffic for pkg-x. If any call pattern deviation or error rate spike, we want an immediate rollback.

legal-bot: license check: both licenses in noise are on procurement_whitelist. No legal block. Tagging manifest: license_whitelist:true.

mia: starting canary in 10. Oncall, when you approve please confirm SHA here (we need it in release notes). If anything changes, we'll pause.

deploybot: CANARY_STARTED rc-2026-c at 2026-09-15T10:20:00Z. metrics: https://metrics/internal/canary/rc-2026-c

deploybot: CANARY ALERT at 2026-09-15T10:45:30Z -> increased error rate on optional path. rolling back to previous artifact per rollback_condition (canary_alerts==true).

mia: rollback initiated. Thanks all for quick responses. Please file postmortem notes if we find root cause.

hannah: Security: monitoring indicates anomaly coincident with new package usage. We'll open INF-4500 with observations.

jorge: oncall recorded approval and evidence but we still rolled back. I'll update oncall log.

deploybot: ARTIFACT ROLLBACK complete at 2026-09-15T10:48:07Z. promoted previous artifact. `deploybot show-manifest rc-2026-c` shows approval metadata and rollback_reason: "canary_alerts==true" for audit.

mia: closing loop: canary failed -> rollback per agreed rule. We'll coordinate a follow-up patch and reconvene for a re-deploy after mitigation. Thanks everyone.
